newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate inches up at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate inches up at close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up five basis points at 21.25 percent on Tuesday after a late surge in a session where rates were generally low on a strong peso, traders said.
"Rates are low now and it seems some players want to keep them where they are," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.2 centavos weaker at 7.8130/7.8180 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper fell five basis points to close at 23.40 percent.
The absence of pressure seen on the peso on Monday, and lower secondary rates for most of the session led traders to revise previous forecasts of increases in primary rates.

A Reuters survey of nine money market dealers showed an average predicted assignment rate of 22.40 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates), which would be a fall of 53 basis points from ;last week's rate.
"There's still plenty of liquidity. Whereas we had expected some upticks in primary rates, a firmer peso means we now see falls across the board," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico is due to release results of the primary auction at 1930 EST.
Banco de Mexico drained 4.426 billion pesos in surplus liquidity through five auctions to purchase paper, which it assigned at between 22.75 and 23.83 percent.
Traders said government spending of some two billion pesos raised the liquidity surplus in the market, originally estimated at 1.419 billion pesos.
Liquidity of 1.536 billion pesos of liquidity is expected to return to the system on Wednesday.
